newsitem.title: CANADA: Indiana boy hit by hockey puck out of coma.
newsitem.headline: Indiana boy hit by hockey puck out of coma.

text.p: An Indiana boy seriously injured by a flying hockey puck in this Canadian border city regained consciousness on Wednesday after lying in a coma for nearly a week, hospital officials said.
Chad Faulkner, 10, was watching a junior hockey league game last Thursday when a puck bounced off a stick and struck him in the head.
Although conscious, the boy remains in a serious condition in intensive care at the Hotel-Dieu Grace Hospital, spokesman Tim Halford said.
Faulkner and his family, from Batesville, Ind., were in Windsor visiting relatives when they decided to attend the hockey game. The child's injury prompted an outpouring of
affection in his hometown and among residents of Windsor, just across the border from Detroit.
To help pay some of his medical costs, the Windsor Spitfires junior hockey team scheduled a charity game against their Detroit rivals on Friday when they hope to raise up to C$30,000 ($21,900).
The Spitfires also made a deal with a local restaurant to supply the boy's family with free meals. National Hockey League players who once played on the Spitfires sent him hockey sticks.
Local schools have made hand-drawn posters, and cards and letters are flooding into the hospital.
"(The deluge of good wishes) is more than I have ever seen in our hospital certainly," said Halford. "It's probably because he was a young lad enjoying himself...minding his own business."

Windsor firefighters sent Faulkner an official Michael Jordan basketball jersey and the family pastor in Indiana passed a teddy bear around the church for the congregation to hug and then sent it to the boy's bedside.
